claims.text: Conventionally processed MnNiSi-based alloy has irregular microstructural features and only limited or sporadic twin boundaries.
Rapid annealing, quenching, or laser-based thermal processing can produce a uniform nano-twin microstructure in MnNiSi-based material.
Room-temperature testing under a 1–2 T field change is representative of magnetic-refrigeration testing.
Controlling treatment energy input and cooling rate will avoid over-processing.
Nano twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The dislocation-barrier action of nano twins increases ductility.
The induced nano twins are structurally coherent.
Coherent nano twins do not significantly disrupt magnetic exchange interactions in MnNiSi-based material.
A primarily structural modification can leave the magnetic entropy change largely unaffected.
The treated material will have greater tensile ductility than untreated MnNiSi.
The treated material will have greater fatigue strength or fatigue life than untreated MnNiSi.
The treated material's magnetic entropy change will remain within approximately 10% of the untreated value.
Conventionally processed untreated MnNiSi has moderate mechanical performance.
Conventionally processed untreated MnNiSi has a large magnetocaloric effect suitable for refrigeration.
An optimal window of treatment energy density, duration, and cooling rate exists in which both benefits are retained.
Excessively severe rapid treatment can degrade mechanical or magnetocaloric performance.
The proposed benefits may not apply to substantially different MnNiSi-based compositions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires ΔS to remain within approximately 10% of baseline, whereas falsification is triggered only by a reduction exceeding an ambiguous 10–20% range. A reduction between 10% and 20% could violate the prediction without unambiguously falsifying the hypothesis.
